title: Old band music: New Orleans Jazz and other parts handed over
summary: Looking through his band music, they find New Orleans Jazz and other parts; he gives a piece to the interviewer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You have some of the music there, too.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. Can I see what pieces they played there? I didn't know this was any of it, see. That might have been some of the music, see.
Oh, look, the first piece we pick up is called New Orleans Jazz.
Yeah, I was crazy about that piece, and I always, I always kept that piece, you see.

Look at that, New Orleans Jazz. Yeah. My Desi left. There's a piece of music, too. One Step by Don Richards, and this happens to be the B-flat soprano sax part. Yeah. Published by Leo Feist. It doesn't give the date. And the other parts are from the same piece, except here's one more number called the Royal Scotch Highlanders, a march. And we have the third and fourth E-flat alto parts. It's by K.L. King. I forget the publisher. The publisher's mark is torn off here.
Now, if those pieces would do you any good, I can mark my name on the back of them, and you can have those.

Well, I'll tell you, let's take one of them anyway. We'll take one, uh... That New Orleans Jazz? ...this one New Orleans Jazz, and we don't want to take all of them, because you might want to give them to somebody else, too.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. Now, this here, this here, I don't know about that.
Now, here's the first clarinet part, or the E-flat clarinet.

Well, I didn't play the E-flat, I played the B-flat. I just kept on, you know, just because of, well, remembrance or something. Never been. It might be pieces. I know this is one, I really, really did like that New Orleans Jazz. It's the H-flat.
If you're sure you don't need that. No, I won't need that.
We don't want to take it if you'll be never playing it again. Well, I don't think of my days is too long now.
Well, I hope, I hope you live a long time.
